outcome: maternal complications (abruptio placenta, PPH, pulmonary edema, maternal mortality)
fetal/neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, IUD, stillbirth, infant mortality)
cohort: 170 participants with singleton pregnancies complicated by pregnancy induced hypertension at a tertiary care center.
finding: The study found a 9.5% incidence rate of PIH, with preeclampsia being the most common type, and reported specific rates for various maternal complications (e.g., abruptio placenta 4.7%, maternal mortality 0.6%) and neonatal adverse outcomes (e.g., low birth weight 52.4%, IUD 5.9%).
cross-section timing: Data collected over a period of one and a half year.
